newsitem.title: CROATIA: Part of Croatia's biggest refinery modernised.
newsitem.headline: Part of Croatia's biggest refinery modernised.

text.p: The Croatian state oil company INA modernised a plant for desulphurisation of diesel fuel at the country's biggest refinery in the Adriatic port of Rijeka, local media reported on Friday.

The plant will enable the refinery to produce diesel fuel with only 0.05 percent of sulphur -- 20 times less than before -- to suit European ecological standards, daily newspaper Slobodna Dalmacija said.
"With this (plant), Croatia is becoming competitive in the world market," Croatian radio quoted President Franjo Tudjman, who opened the modernised plant, as saying.
President of INA's supervisory board Hrvoje Sarinic put the Rijeka investment at a total of 500 million kuna ($84 million), of which some was used for maintenance work.
It was said to be the first major investment in the refinery in 16 years. Engineering work was done by INA-Projekt of the INA group.
"This is an important energy saver and will contribute to safety at work and environment protection," Sarinic said.
Maintenance work, including replacing old equipment at two platforms, will be completed by June 30, he said.
